record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: For a polynomial automorphism f of C^d with d≥3, describe the growth type of the sequence deg(f^n).

evidence.quote: Problem 8. — Describe the growth type of the sequence {deg(fn)} for any polynomial automorphism f of Cd, d ≥ 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$ and let $f : \mathbb{C}^d \to \mathbb{C}^d$ be a polynomial automorphism, i.e., a bijective map whose components and the components of whose inverse are polynomials in $d$ complex variables. For a polynomial map $g = (g_1, \dots, g_d) : \mathbb{C}^d \to \mathbb{C}^d$, define the degree of $g$ by $\deg(g) = \max_{1 \le i \le d} \deg(g_i)$, where $\deg(g_i)$ is the total degree of the polynomial $g_i$. Let $f^n = f \circ f \circ \cdots \circ f$ denote the $n$-fold iterate of $f$.

Describe, as completely as possible, the possible asymptotic growth types of the sequence $\{\deg(f^n)\}_{n \ge 1}$ as $n \to \infty$, ranging over all polynomial automorphisms $f$ of $\mathbb{C}^d$. In particular, classify which growth behaviors (e.g., bounded, polynomial of given degree, exponential with prescribed rate, intermediate types) can arise, and for each such type characterize the automorphisms $f$ realizing it.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of degree growth of polynomial automorphisms of $\mathbb{C}^d$ is well understood for $d=2$ (work of Friedland–Milnor and others), but for $d \ge 3$ the problem remains open in general. Recent advances (e.g., optimal bounds on polynomial volume growth in terms of $d^2$ for zero-entropy automorphisms of projective varieties) provide partial information on possible polynomial growth rates, but a complete classification of growth types in higher dimensions has not been achieved.

status_evidence.title: An Upper Bound for Polynomial Volume Growth of Automorphisms of Zero Entropy
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal bound that polynomial volume growth is bounded by d^2 for automorphisms of dimension d, answering questions of Cantat–Paris-Romaskevich and Lin–Oguiso–Zhang.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on polynomial growth rates in higher dimensions has been made, but a full description remains open.
